From 458d5615272d3de535748342eb68ca492343048c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jamal Hadi Salim <jhs@mojatatu.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Apr 2026 11:29:55 -0400
Subject: [PATCH] net/sched: sch_red: Replace direct dequeue call with peek and
 qdisc_dequeue_peeked

When red qdisc has children (eg qfq qdisc) whose peek() callback is
qdisc_peek_dequeued(), we could get a kernel panic. When the parent of such
qdiscs (eg illustrated in patch #3 as tbf) wants to retrieve an skb from
its child (red in this case), it will do the following:
 1a. do a peek() - and when sensing there's an skb the child can offer, then
     - the child in this case(red) calls its child's (qfq) peek.
        qfq does the right thing and will return the gso_skb queue packet.
        Note: if there wasnt a gso_skb entry then qfq will store it there.
 1b. invoke a dequeue() on the child (red). And herein lies the problem.
     - red will call the child's dequeue() which will essentially just
       try to grab something of qfq's queue.

The right thing to do in #1b is to grab the skb off gso_skb queue.
This patchset fixes that issue by changing #1b to use qdisc_dequeue_peeked()
method instead.

Fixes: 77be155cba4e ("pkt_sched: Add peek emulation for non-work-conserving qdiscs.")
Reported-by: Manas <ghandatmanas@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Rakshit Awasthi <rakshitawasthi17@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jamal Hadi Salim <jhs@mojatatu.com>
Reviewed-by: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260430152957.194015-2-jhs@mojatatu.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/sched/sch_red.c b/net/sched/sch_red.c
index 432b8a3000a5..4d0e44a2e7c6 100644
--- a/net/sched/sch_red.c
+++ b/net/sched/sch_red.c
@@ -162,7 +162,7 @@ static struct sk_buff *red_dequeue(struct Qdisc *sch)
 	struct red_sched_data *q = qdisc_priv(sch);
 	struct Qdisc *child = q->qdisc;
 
-	skb = child->dequeue(child);
+	skb = qdisc_dequeue_peeked(child);
 	if (skb) {
 		qdisc_bstats_update(sch, skb);
 		qdisc_qstats_backlog_dec(sch, skb);
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies only one file: `net/sched/sch_red.c`. The change replaces a direct call to `child->dequeue(child)` with a call to `qdisc_dequeue_peeked(child)`. This fix addresses a kernel panic that occurs when RED qdisc has children (e.g., QFQ) whose `peek()` callback uses `qdisc_peek_dequeued()`. The direct dequeue incorrectly attempts to grab a packet from the child’s queue, while `qdisc_dequeue_peeked()` correctly retrieves the skb from the `gso_skb` queue that was stored during the peek operation, avoiding a null-pointer dereference. The relationship is straightforward: the single-line change in the `red_dequeue` function fixes a specific bug in the dequeue logic when dealing with non-work-conserving child qdiscs.

Here is the root cause:
In red_dequeue(), the direct call to child->dequeue(child) bypasses the proper handling of the peeked skb stored in gso_skb by qdisc_peek_dequeued(). When the child qdisc (e.g., qfq) uses qdisc_peek_dequeued(), the peek stores the skb in gso_skb, but the subsequent dequeue from red incorrectly calls child->dequeue(), which attempts to dequeue from the regular queue rather than returning the already-peeked skb, leading to a null-pointer dereference.

Here is the patch:
 
 static struct sk_buff *red_dequeue(struct Qdisc *sch)
 {
 	struct sk_buff *skb;
 	struct red_sched_data *q = qdisc_priv(sch);
 	struct Qdisc *child = q->qdisc;
 
-	skb = child->dequeue(child);
+	skb = qdisc_dequeue_peeked(child);
 	if (skb) {
 		qdisc_bstats_update(sch, skb);
 		qdisc_qstats_backlog_dec(sch, skb);
 		sch->q.qlen--;
 	} else {
 		if (!red_is_idling(&q->vars))
 			red_start_of_idle_period(&q->vars);
 	}
 	return skb;
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```
skb = child->dequeue(child);
```
Reason:
When RED’s child qdisc (e.g., QFQ) uses `qdisc_peek_dequeued()`, a peek call stores the skb in `gso_skb`. However, `red_dequeue()` directly invokes `child->dequeue(child)`, which bypasses the stored peeked skb and attempts to dequeue from the regular queue. This causes a null-pointer dereference if the regular queue is empty or in an inconsistent state.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```
skb = qdisc_dequeue_peeked(child);
```
Reason:
`qdisc_dequeue_peeked()` correctly returns the skb that was previously peeked and stored in `gso_skb`, avoiding the inconsistent state. It replaces the direct dequeue call, ensuring the proper flow for qdiscs that implement the peek emulation mechanism.
